column1: # source: Trevino & Allen 2013, Within-consonant perceptual differences in the hearing impaired ear, JASA 134(1):607-617, doi:10.1121/1.4807474, Table III; open text PMC3732204 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3732204/), cells parsed from the article's HTML table 2026-10-15.

# 17 ears of 9 hearing-impaired American English listeners (Urbana-Champaign; mostly slight-to-moderate high-frequency sloping sensorineural loss, one ear with an inverted loss; every ear >20 dB HL at some frequency 0.25-4 kHz), no hearing aid, flat gain at most comfortable level. 14 consonants + /a/ from the LDC Articulation Index corpus (LDC2005S22), one female (F) and one male (M) token each (f: female token only in this table), closed-set response.

# condition: average over the 17 ears and 4 speech-weighted noise conditions (0, +6, +12 dB SNR, quiet). Rows = token (consonant_talker), columns = heard, percent. Cells under 2% are not shown in the paper (blank), written 0 here, so rows sum to about 90-100. sh = /S/, zh = /Z/.
